rules.title: `from` is a contextual keyword in `use … from <module>;`
rules.statement: In `use pkg from <module-expr>;`, `from` is lexed as a plain IDENT token (not a reserved keyword) and validated to equal the text "from" during semantic analysis; a global reserved keyword `from` would clash with the `From::from` trait method name.

rules.title: `?Trait` relaxed bound accepts only `?Sized`
rules.statement: A TRAIT_BOUND may carry a RELAXED marker for the `?Trait` relaxed-bound syntax; in the current phase the only accepted relaxed bound is `?Sized`.

rules.title: Raw-text macro-call capture honours backslash and backtick escapes
rules.statement: RAW_TEXT captured from a balanced brace-delimited group on a fn-macro call (RAW_GROUP_*) honours two escapes so literal braces don't break brace balancing: (a) a backslash immediately preceding `{`, `}`, backtick, or `\` passes that character through without counting it toward the balance (the backslash itself survives into the captured text, for the handler to de-escape); (b) a backtick-delimited region is skipped as a whole, with no brace counting performed inside it. Both are additive: a well-formed body without these constructs is captured byte-identically.

rules.title: `pub(module)` vs plain `pub` visibility
rules.statement: An item declaration's visibility is carried by a VIS sub-node: NAME="module" denotes `pub(module)` (module-linkage visibility); an absent NAME denotes plain `pub`.

rules.title: `@{...}` meta block on struct/datatype/trait declarations
rules.statement: struct, datatype, and trait declarations may carry a `@{...}` META sub-node attached at the item level.
rules.uncertainty: This slice only shows the field-slot assignment and its purpose comment; the internal grammar of the `@{...}` block body is not shown here.

rules.title: `code(expr)` clause on schema declarations
rules.statement: SCHEMA_DEF and SCHEMA_ENUM_DEF declarations accept a `code(expr)` clause, represented as a sub-node with NAME="code", VALUE=expr.

rules.title: `use pkg.Path.Type.{V1, V2, …};` imports selected enum variants
rules.statement: A USE_VARIANTS import form `use pkg.Path.Type.{V1, V2, …};` binds the listed variant names of enum Type into scope; its AST carries TYPE_NAME (the enum type reference) and VARIANTS (an array of variant-name sub-nodes).

rules.title: `#ident` antiquotation placeholder inside `quote_*!` bodies
rules.statement: Inside the body of a `quote_*!` macro, `#ident` is an antiquotation placeholder splicing an external value; its AST node carries a NAME_VAR field holding the placeholder's identifier text. NAME_VAR exists only inside quote_*! bodies (where a where-clause never co-occurs).

rules.title: `impl !Trait for Type {}` negative implementation
rules.statement: `impl !Trait for Type {}` is parsed as an IMPL_BLOCK carrying an IS_NEGATIVE marker, denoting a negative trait implementation (an explicit opt-out of Trait for Type).

rules.title: `for<'a, 'b>` higher-ranked binder on a trait bound
rules.statement: A TRAIT_BOUND may carry a `for<'a, 'b, …>` higher-ranked lifetime binder list, represented as an HRTB_BINDERS sub-node whose ITEMS are LIFETIME_PARAM entries.

rules.title: N-deep field-chain write path
rules.statement: An assignment through an N-deep chain of field accesses (e.g. `a.b.c = expr;`) is represented with a PATH sub-node carrying ITEMS=[str, ...] naming the successive field components of the chain.
rules.uncertainty: This slice shows only the field-slot comment for the chain-write PATH sub-node, not the statement's full grammar production.

rules.title: Qualified CALL/GENERIC_CALL carries package-path segments
rules.statement: A qualified CALL or GENERIC_CALL node may carry QUAL_PARTS: package-path segments following RECEIVER, supporting fully-qualified dotted-package call syntax (e.g. `pkg.sub::func(...)`); call nodes never populate a plain module USES field simultaneously, so QUAL_PARTS reuses that slot.

rules.title: Struct-shaped enum variant marker
rules.statement: An enum VARIANT_DEF (and correspondingly ENUM_LIT_DATA / PAT_VARIANT_DATA) may carry an IS_STRUCT_SHAPE marker distinguishing a struct-shaped variant (braced named fields) from a tuple-shaped variant.
